description: Australian accounting engines, sourced tax worksheets and local MCP and command-line adapters. Independently versioned components with explicit scope, supported years, warnings and refusal codes.
rules: Select the component and its documented interface first. Components have independent versions and releases; repository main is not proof that a capability is in an installed distribution.
For a regular pay, use the PAYG withholding worksheet for the employee's pay period and scale. Do not apply annual tax brackets to a single pay or treat annual assessed tax as withholding.

Supply explicit supported years and all required scope confirmations. When an interface supports pay dates, preserve its date/year consistency checks and within-year rule selection. Never infer support for a future year.
Use decimal strings for money and ratios at the native JSON boundary. Respect the selected engine's rounding and output units rather than reimplementing tax formulas in an adapter.

Retain engine version, sources, warnings and refusal codes. A refused or unsupported calculation stays refused; never replace it with a plausible estimate without explicitly changing the task and its stated assumptions.

Ordinary PAYG, study-loan withholding, special payments, Medicare levy and Medicare levy surcharge have distinct scopes. Use only the inputs and combinations documented for the selected worksheet and version.
Use fabricated fixtures for examples. Do not send TFNs, client data or other private financial inputs to public calculators, URLs or hosted checkers.

A worksheet supports human review; it is not an assessment or lodgment. Distinguish a super accrual from evidence of receipt by a fund and distinguish a planning assumption from a statutory calculation.
